source.title: Entropy-SGD optimizes the prior of a PAC-Bayes bound: Data-dependent PAC-Bayes priors via differential privacy

record.tranche_reason: Tests the coexistence of natural-label generalization and random-label overfitting using SGD, SGLD, Entropy-SGD and Entropy-SGLD, with different noise settings and architectures.
record.gate_note: Reports the study's own outcomes for true and random labels, including training and held-out errors. Cited findings from earlier work are not recorded as results. Values reported only in figures are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study measures training and held-out errors on fixed random and natural labels under several optimization recipes, bearing on V1. Its convolutional versus fully connected comparisons also test V3 in an Entropy-SGLD setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially correct. Entropy-SGD optimizes a data-dependent prior, invalidating the naive PAC-Bayes guarantee, and can fit random labels. Adding outer-loop noise yields Entropy-SGLD, which can suppress random-label overfitting and produce nonvacuous bounds under an assumed convergence condition. These bounds are optimistic; learning is slower and test performance remains worse than SGD.
record.recipe_differences: Studies Entropy-SGD and a modified Entropy-SGLD with added outer-loop SGLD noise, alongside SGD and SGLD; uses two-class and multiclass MNIST and CIFAR10 experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Thermal noise and τ affect the risk/generalization tradeoff and random-label overfitting; results differ across architectures and datasets. The text reports FC600 and FC1200 results are nearly identical despite a threefold parameter difference.

fits_no_version.finding: FC600 and FC1200 have nearly identical errors and bounds despite an approximately threefold parameter-count difference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Two tested fully connected widths can perform similarly under Entropy-SGLD without establishing behavior beyond interpolation.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 80, 2018
record.problems: The study assumes SGLD has converged when reporting its bounds; the authors call those bounds optimistic. Several error values are available only in figures. The results are on the paper's own settings and architectures, not all settings named in the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: CIFAR10 experiments report additional τ and γ sweeps in Figures 5 and 6, but precise values and condition-to-value assignments are figure-only in the supplied text; omitted to avoid reconstructing values from plots. The multiclass MNIST true-label comparisons in Figure 4 are not separately rowed because their text describes the generalization gap qualitatively without reporting distinct test-error values.

untested.parts: The original named architectures and ImageNet setting are not tested. Several extracted random-label rows do not quantify near-perfect fitting.
No width sweep beyond an established zero-training-error threshold.
Local connectivity as the explanation, learned sparse connections, convolution-derived initialization, and architecture comparisons under ordinary SGD are not established here.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No controlled comparison of dropout settings.
No magnitude-scaled sharpness ranking against generalization gaps and competing measures.
No removal and retraining experiment based on example memorization.

missing.what: The study explicitly reports zero random-label training error for available Entropy-SGD implementations and their Gibbs posteriors. Record this full-fit evidence separately without assigning it indiscriminately to every noise setting.
missing.locator: Abstract; Introduction; Discussion identifies overfitting at thermal noise 0.0001

missing.what: The multiclass MNIST architecture comparison explicitly states that CONV has lower training and test errors than FC1024. The declared omission of true-label gaps does not capture this V3 result.

SGLD has high random-label generalization error at thermal noise 0.01 and below, paired with small empirical risk at low noise and small natural-label gaps. These qualitative results do not require reconstructing plot values.

record.verdict_notes: Generalization error in this paper usually denotes the train–population error gap. A small gap on random labels reflects failure to memorize, not successful prediction. The study is not an original source for these versions. CIFAR10 sweeps and multiclass true-label gap results were declared omitted in rows_left_out and are not listed as new missing results.

versions.untested_parts: The named Zhang et al. architectures and ImageNet/Inception V3 setting are not tested. The paper tests two-class and multiclass MNIST and CIFAR10 with its own architectures and algorithms.

The paper compares CONV with fully connected networks on MNIST, but does not test whether local connectivity accounts for the advantage, sparse local connections, or initialization of a fully connected network from a trained convolutional network.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Entropy-SGD at thermal noise 0.01 on true and random labels.
rows.measure: Training risk and generalization error; text says it achieves good risk and low generalization error on both true and random labels.
rows.value: Good risk and low generalization error on both true and random labels; exact values figure only
rows.note: The text says the test-set performance at this setting is still worse than SGD.
rows.check: Low generalization error means a small train–population error gap, not accurate prediction of random labels. This setting avoids substantial random-label memorization and therefore does not support V1's coexistence result. Split natural and random labels into separate rows.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Entropy-SGD at thermal noise 0.005 and below on random labels.
rows.measure: Training and test 0–1 error; text says Entropy-SGD overfits.
rows.value: Overfits for thermal noise values 0.005 and below; exact values figure only
rows.note: The figure caption says the random-label thermal-noise 0.01 setting performs well on both true and random labels.
rows.check: Random-label overfitting is consistent with V1, rather than a failure of it. The row does not quantify whether fitting is nearly perfect; the abstract separately reports zero random-label training error for available Entropy-SGD implementations.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for this row's almost-perfect-fitting endpoint. The abstract separately establishes zero random-label training error for available Entropy-SGD implementations without assigning that endpoint to every listed thermal-noise setting.
source_check.problem: Unquantified overfitting does not establish the incomplete fitting implied by partial.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Entropy-SGLD at τ = √m on true labels.
rows.measure: Training and test 0–1 error for mean and Gibbs classifiers; generalization gap.
rows.value: Both classifiers have approximately 2% test error and essentially zero generalization error
rows.note: The paper evaluates both a deterministic mean classifier and its associated randomized Gibbs classifier.
rows.check: Establishes natural-label performance only. Approximately 2% test error and a negligible gap imply approximately 2% training error; R6 shows this recipe does not also memorize random labels.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V1 coexistence from this natural-label-only row; R6 separately establishes absent random-label memorization under the same recipe.
source_check.problem: The observed state describes natural-label learning rather than the linked version's coexistence effect.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Entropy-SGLD at τ = √m on random labels.
rows.value: Does not overfit, even after thousands of epochs
rows.note: The figure caption also states that Entropy-SGLD does not overfit on random labels.
rows.check: Absence of random-label overfitting is absence of V1's memorization component, not an observed coexistence effect.

rows.subject: FC1024
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Entropy-SGLD on random labels.
rows.measure: Training and test 0–1 error; generalization gap.
rows.value: After approximately 1000 epochs, overfitting by ≈ 2%; further training does not cause additional overfitting
rows.note: This is a small but explicitly reported random-label generalization gap.
rows.check: A roughly two-percentage-point random-label gap is only weak memorization, far short of nearly perfect random-label fitting.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Entropy-SGLD on random labels.
rows.value: Almost no overfitting (less than 1%); training and test error coincide and remain close to the guessing rate (90%)
rows.note: The reported errors remain near the guessing rate rather than showing natural-label generalization.
rows.check: The authors describe the less-than-one-percentage-point gap as almost no overfitting; training and test errors remain near 90%. Treat this as negligible memorization.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Compared convolutional and fully connected architectures trained on true labels.
rows.measure: Training and test errors; generalization bounds.
rows.value: CONV produces the lowest training and test errors and tightest generalization bounds
rows.note: The paper does not attribute the difference specifically to local connectivity.
rows.check: Lower test error supports the architecture comparison. Tighter bounds are a separate finding and do not themselves establish better generalization.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.2, opening paragraph; Appendix C; Figure 2.

rows.subject: FC600
rows.operation_detail: Compared with FC1200 on true labels.
rows.measure: Training and test errors; generalization bounds.
rows.value: Results are nearly identical to FC1200 despite FC1200 having three times as many parameters
rows.note: This width comparison does not establish behavior past an interpolation threshold.
rows.check: This row compares two fully connected widths, not convolutional and fully connected networks. It also does not establish zero training error or a post-interpolation width regime required by V2.

rows.subject: FC1200
rows.operation_detail: Compared with FC600 on true labels.
rows.measure: Training and test errors; generalization bounds.
rows.value: Results are nearly identical to FC600 despite having three times as many parameters
rows.note: This width comparison does not establish behavior past an interpolation threshold.
rows.check: Duplicates the FC600–FC1200 comparison in R10 and supplies no independent V3 comparison or V2 interpolation evidence.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGLD at thermal noise 0.05 on true and random labels.
rows.measure: Risk and generalization error; text says SGLD achieves reasonable but relatively large risk and almost zero generalization error on both true and random labels.
rows.value: Almost zero generalization error on both true and random labels
rows.note: The stated tradeoff is that risk is relatively large.
rows.check: Almost zero generalization gap on random labels means little memorization, not support for coexistence. Split natural and random labels; retain the relatively large natural-label risk qualification.
